page: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine engineered for large-scale parallel computing and machine learning tasks. The configuration features 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs based on the Ampere architecture, delivering a combined total of 320 GB of GPU memory. The host system is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, providing 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 38 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 extensions, and 680.0 GB of system memory.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity across parallelized and accelerator workloads. The system achieves top-tier results in large language model inference across 7B and 70B parameter models for both prompt processing and token generation. Multi-core performance metrics are robust, reflected in high stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores, alongside memory read bandwidth reaching 219.95 GB/sec on large blocks and 64.13 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-threaded execution is relatively modest, as shown by lower Geekbench single-core and single-threaded compression scores.

Because the instance includes no local storage, storage operations rely entirely on attached network volumes. Resource allocation favors multi-threaded parallel throughput and GPU execution over single-core speed. From an infrastructure cost perspective, this configuration aggregates immense accelerator and memory density into a single host, maximizing hardware utilization for workloads that can saturate eight GPUs simultaneously.

The a2-highgpu-8g instance is suited for deep learning training, distributed LLM inference, molecular modeling, high-performance computing simulations, and high-throughput data processing pipelines requiring high GPU and host memory density.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized instance designed for intensive distributed computing and deep learning workloads. The system integrates 8 NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with 320 GB of collective VRAM alongside an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores at 2.2 GHz. System memory totals 680.0 GB, providing 7.08 GB per vCPU core. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier execution in LLM prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and 70B parameter models, accompanied by high multi-core throughput and strong large-block memory read bandwidth. Single-core compute and compression metrics demonstrate lower relative performance, reflecting its parallel optimization. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage, requiring attached network disks. This hardware profile is suited for large-scale AI model training, parallel inference pipelines, and compute-heavy scientific simulation workloads.
